title: Algorithmic Foundations
focus: Asymptotic reasoning, core data structures, graph algorithms, sorting, and tractability as practical design tools.

pacing.review: Skim the mechanism sections and run the lab once.
pacing.standard: Study all lessons, complete exercises, run the lab, and explain each tradeoff in your own words.
pacing.deep: Extend the lab with one additional data structure or graph workload.

learning_outcomes.statement: Use Big-O, theta, omega, and amortized analysis without confusing them for measured runtime.
Choose arrays, linked structures, hash tables, trees, heaps, or graphs from workload shape and invariants.
Explain why locality, hashing assumptions, balancing, and priority semantics change system behavior.
Recognize graph, sorting, selection, and intractable subproblems inside system-design work.
Measure a local algorithmic claim and state what the measurement does and does not prove.

lab.note: Run the deterministic complexity harness to compare logical operations, locality-sensitive traversal, and hash lookup assumptions.

optional_project.description: Analyze a data-heavy workflow you know, name the hidden algorithmic decisions, and replace one assumption with a measurement.

resources.title: Open Data Structures
resources.purpose: Use chapters on arrays, lists, hash tables, trees, heaps, and graphs as a precise reference.

resources.title: CLRS Lecture Notes
resources.purpose: Review formal treatments for asymptotic analysis, sorting, hashing, and graph traversal.

resources.title: What Every Programmer Should Know About Memory
resources.purpose: Connect algorithmic access patterns to cache, locality, and memory latency.

resources.title: Computational Complexity
resources.purpose: Use as a readable reference for P, NP, reductions, and why intractability changes engineering choices.
